common_name: Pacifica XP Really Red Vinca (Disease-Resistant Scarlet Annual Vinca)

planting.note: Set out transplants once nights stay reliably above 55F and soil has warmed, since chilled roots stall growth for weeks. Pacifica XP was bred for a tight, uniform bloom window, so a whole flat finishes together for even bedding displays.

directions: Give Pacifica XP Really Red a full-sun bed with sharp drainage, since the XP breeding line still needs dry-sided soil even though it resists Phytophthora far better than heirloom vinca strains. The upright, rounded habit holds saturated scarlet-red blooms just above glossy foliage from late spring straight through the first hard frost without any deadheading. It shrugs off the punishing heat and humidity that wilts petunias and impatiens, making it a dependable centerpiece color for mixed beds or large containers. Skip overhead watering late in the day and let the top inch of soil dry between waterings to keep root rot pressure low.

common_name: Pacifica XP Deep Orchid Vinca (Disease-Resistant Lavender-Purple Annual Vinca)

planting.note: Delay transplanting until soil and night air are consistently warm, since Pacifica XP sulks and yellows in cold, damp spring soil. The series was bred for programmable, even flowering, so it fills beds uniformly within a few weeks of planting.

directions: Pacifica XP Deep Orchid carries rich lavender-purple flowers over dark, glossy foliage on a compact, mounded plant that holds its shape without staking. Plant in full sun and well-drained soil; the XP line's improved tolerance to aerial and soilborne Phytophthora makes it noticeably more forgiving than older vinca strains during humid Gulf Coast summers. Water at the soil line and allow the surface to dry between irrigations, since consistently soggy crowns are the main cause of vinca collapse even in resistant cultivars. Once established it needs no fertilizer beyond an initial feeding and no deadheading to bloom nonstop into fall.

common_name: Pacifica XP Icy Pink Vinca (Disease-Resistant Pale Pink Annual Vinca)

planting.note: Hold transplants until nighttime lows are dependably above 55F; vinca set out too early simply stalls until the ground warms rather than growing on. Pacifica XP Icy Pink flowers quickly and evenly once conditions are right, filling beds fast.

directions: Pacifica XP Icy Pink produces soft blush-pink blooms with a faint deeper pink eye on a compact, upright plant that reads almost white from a distance and brightens shady-adjacent full-sun beds. Site it in full sun with fast-draining soil, since the XP breeding improves but does not eliminate the vinca family's vulnerability to root and stem rot in soggy ground. It thrives through the hottest, most humid stretch of summer when many bedding annuals decline, and needs no regular deadheading or fertilizing to keep blooming to frost. Let the soil surface dry between waterings and avoid mulching directly against the crown.

common_name: Cora Cascade Polka Dot Vinca (Trailing Bicolor Disease-Resistant Annual Vinca)

planting.note: Transplant into hanging baskets, window boxes, or bed edges once the soil has warmed well past the last frost date. Cora Cascade Polka Dot carries the same aerial Phytophthora resistance bred into the upright Cora XDR line, in a trailing habit.

directions: Crisp white petals with a bold dark-pink eye give Cora Cascade Polka Dot a bicolor punch that stands out in mixed hanging baskets and spilling over raised bed edges. Grow it in full sun with well-drained potting mix or garden soil; the trailing stems cascade eighteen to twenty-five inches without pinching and stay fuller through summer heat than older trailing vinca lines. Its disease resistance to aerial Phytophthora blight makes it far more reliable than heirloom trailing vinca in the humid, rain-prone conditions of a Gulf Coast summer. Water at the base rather than overhead and let containers approach dryness between waterings to avoid crown rot.

common_name: Cora XDR Cranberry Vinca (Extra Disease-Resistant Deep Red Annual Vinca)

planting.note: Set transplants out only once soil has warmed thoroughly after the last frost, since cold snaps stunt vinca for weeks afterward. Cora XDR was bred for the broadest resistance yet to aerial Phytophthora isolates, making it a dependable choice for wet summers.

directions: Cora XDR Cranberry produces large, deep burgundy-red flowers with a small white eye over glossy, mounded foliage, giving beds a saturated jewel-tone color that holds up under full summer sun. Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; the XDR breeding line carries resistance to a wider range of aerial Phytophthora strains than earlier Cora selections, which matters most in humid, rainy stretches when older vinca varieties collapse overnight. It blooms continuously from late spring to frost with no deadheading required and tolerates drought once roots are established. Avoid heavy mulch pressed against the stems and water the soil rather than the foliage to keep disease pressure low.

common_name: Mediterranean XP Strawberry Vinca (Trailing Bicolor Annual Vinca)

planting.note: Plant out into baskets, window boxes, or bed fronts once the soil is thoroughly warm past the last frost date. Mediterranean XP was bred for a fast, uniform fill and a tight flowering window compared to older trailing vinca seed lines.

directions: Mediterranean XP Strawberry spreads twenty to thirty inches wide on a low, mounded plant just a few inches tall, making it one of the best low-growing spillers for full-sun containers and hanging baskets. Its rosy-pink flowers with a subtle darker eye keep coming nonstop through the hottest, most humid weeks of summer, when many trailing annuals fade. Grow it in fast-draining potting mix or garden soil in full sun, and let the surface dry between waterings since trailing vinca is just as prone to crown rot as upright types in soggy conditions. Once roots fill the container it tolerates real drought stress and needs no deadheading to keep flowering to frost.

common_name: Mediterranean XP Burgundy Halo Vinca (Trailing Dark-Eyed Annual Vinca)

planting.note: Wait until soil has fully warmed after the last frost before setting out transplants, since trailing vinca stalls in cold ground just like upright types. Mediterranean XP Burgundy Halo fills baskets and beds quickly once nights are reliably warm.

directions: Mediterranean XP Burgundy Halo shows pale petals ringed by a distinct dark burgundy halo around each flower's center, adding contrast to trailing baskets and ground-covering beds. The plant stays a few inches tall while trailing up to thirty inches, making full use of container edges and slopes in full sun. Plant in well-drained soil, water at the base, and allow the surface to dry between waterings, since trailing vinca is prone to the same crown and root rot as upright vinca in soggy sites. It is exceptionally heat- and drought-tolerant once established and blooms without interruption from late spring through the first fall frost.

common_name: Jams 'N Jellies Blackberry Vinca (AAS-Winning Velvet Purple Annual Vinca)

planting.note: Start seed indoors and hold transplants until nights stay reliably above 55F, since this compact AAS winner stalls in cool, damp spring soil like all annual vinca. It bulks up quickly once truly warm weather arrives.

directions: Jams 'N Jellies Blackberry is an All-America Selections winner prized for a flower color unlike any other vinca on the market: velvety, near-black deep purple petals set off by a small white eye. The compact, well-branched plant holds its two-inch blooms above dark green foliage from early summer straight through frost without deadheading. Grow it in full sun with well-drained soil, since it shares the broader vinca family's vulnerability to root and stem rot in cold or waterlogged ground despite its excellent heat and drought tolerance. Its unusual dark coloring makes it a striking accent against silver-leaved or bright chartreuse companion plants in beds and containers.

common_name: Jams 'N Jellies Blueberry Vinca (Deep Violet-Blue Annual Vinca)

planting.note: Delay transplanting until soil is thoroughly warm after the last frost date, since chilled roots stunt this compact series for weeks. Jams N Jellies Blueberry fills in quickly once nights are dependably warm.

directions: Jams N Jellies Blueberry pairs with its Blackberry series-mate to bring an unusual deep violet-blue tone into the vinca color range, sitting atop a compact, mounding plant that needs no staking. Plant in full sun and well-drained soil, since even this novelty color retains the vinca family's dislike of cold, soggy ground and benefits from raised beds or amended soil in heavy clay. It flowers nonstop from early summer to frost without deadheading and tolerates heat and drought better than most other bedding annuals, making it a reliable filler for hot, exposed sites. Space plants to allow good airflow between them, since crowding raises the risk of fungal disease during humid weather.
